summary.headline: Shadowfax Q1 FY27 revenue rose 65% YoY to INR1,358 crore; management raised FY27 growth guidance to 38-40% from 27-30%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 65% YoY to INR1,358 crore and 10% QoQ, the fifth straight quarter of 65%+ growth. Adjusted EBITDA rose to INR67 crore (4.9% margin vs 4.7% in Q4) and PAT hit a record INR65 crore. Management attributed margin gains to lower lost-shipment costs (5.5% of revenue vs 6.1% in Q4) and efficiency work that absorbed diesel and labour cost pressure. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 38-40% while keeping the margin trajectory unchanged.

financial_highlights.change: vs 6.1% in Q4 and 7.9% a year ago
front-loaded ahead of peak season; 77% in network and automation
vs 27-29% last quarter (as cited by analyst)

segments.name: Express Parcel
segments.commentary: Management cites share gains from consolidation between two large 3PL networks; pin codes at ~16,372 after adding ~716 in last 90 days. Prime (same/next-day D2C) grew 2.7x YoY with 400+ D2C customers; SF 360 self-serve has 1,200+ transacting sellers after ~90 days.

segments.name: Prime Large (LCV heavy deliveries)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR75 crore ARR, up close to 170% YoY and 25% QoQ. Reached 10,000 pin codes (FY27 target) in Q1; FY27 target raised to 12,000.

segments.name: Hyperlocal / Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Hyperlocal grew ~53% YoY and 17% QoQ. Amazon Now is a new customer with higher wallet share; Amazon has entered the top-10 customer club.

segments.name: Other logistics services (incl. CriticaLog and dark stores)
segments.commentary: Returned to sequential growth post CriticaLog integration. 47 of 100 planned dark stores live as of 30 June, with 20 more due; dark stores contribute ~10-12% of other logistics services revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to 38-40% from earlier 27-30%; management cites enterprise visibility and new customers.
EBITDA margin trajectory unchanged; management says it will hold the margin guidance given at the start of the year (100-200 bps expansion path per analyst).
Dark store target of 100 for FY27; 47 live as of 30 June.
Prime Large pin code target raised to 12,000 for FY27 from 10,000 (already reached).
Lost shipment cost long-run target 3.5-4% of revenue, from 4.5-5% historically.
Minimum wage hikes in four states add roughly INR2-2.5 crore per month to costs.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex of about INR60 crore, front-loaded before peak season; 77% went to network and automation (sortation centres, machines, IT, electrical).
Added more physical capacity and more pin codes in Q1 than any prior quarter; new pin codes run below capacity initially.
Dark stores live in six metro cities; store sizes range from 200-300 sq ft to 3,000-4,000 sq ft.
No dedicated infrastructure per service line; Prime and Prime Large run on shared hubs and trucks via segmented supply chain software.
demand_pricing: Management says consumption held up better than expected despite diesel price spike, gas supply issues and state elections.
Express market consolidation between two large 3PL networks is shifting volume to Shadowfax; marketplaces expanding into low-value (INR250 order) categories.
Quick commerce outsourcing: management claims 50%+ share of quick commerce outsourcing; industry outsourcing levels 12-15%, with capacity to reach 20-25%.
Express realisation around INR50 per shipment; management says weight, distance and service mix drive it more than Shadowfax controls.
Diesel: contracts allow pass-through, but Shadowfax lagged the increase by 5 days and absorbed the cost.

qa_highlights.question: What supports the raised growth guidance from Q2 to Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhishek Bansal cited enterprise customer forward projections and visibility, plus new D2C and quick commerce customers (Amazon Now); he said the company is fairly confident in the numbers.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 capex is for the growth upgrade versus beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex is front-loaded before the peak season and the product mix is unchanged, with 77% in network and automation; the assets last 5+ years.

qa_highlights.question: Can the margin bridge be explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Praveen Kumar KJ said transport cost rose 0.1 pp to 18.8%, consumables rose 0.1 pp, and other costs rose 0.1 pp; lost-shipment cost fell 0.6 pp to 5.5%. Efficiency work offset larger cost increases; management says most of the cost impact is already in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the minimum wage hike?
qa_highlights.answer: INR2-2.5 crore per month across four states; management said much of the delta does not hit P&L because many staff earn incentives above minimum wage.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 dark store contribution disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined store-wise revenue but said all stores together contribute 10-12% of other logistics services revenue; it will provide more detail as the vertical matures.

qa_highlights.question: Is there cannibalisation between vertical dark-store quick commerce and SDD for D2C?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhishek Bansal said SKU width differs (about 1 million SKUs for same-day vs up to 10,000 for dark-store delivery), so the models serve different needs in the same cities.

risks_watch: Diesel and crude-linked cost pressure; management absorbed a 5-day diesel pass-through lag.
Labour supply squeeze and minimum wage increases (INR2-2.5 crore per month).
Pricing pressure from listed anchor customers, which management says is managed through rate cards with volume-linked discounts.
Dependence on two large Express 3PL networks and on Amazon Now ramp-up.
Dark store economics still unproven at store level; 47 live of 100 target by year-end.
Upside growth guidance depends on new customer acquisition and sales-season volumes.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive. Management was assertive on raising guidance and on market-share gains, but gave limited numbers on dark stores, realisation and the margin bridge, and deflected some questions on pricing and realisation to external factors.
key_quotes: Through all of it, our performance effectively showed zero volatility.
We were not going to let the external environment decide our margins.
